title: Operator funnel metrics + trace heuristics (working notes)
summary: Working notes for mapping user/operator funnels to compact dashboard tiles and trace annotation heuristics. Goal: make triage fast for SREs and support engineers while keeping query cost bounded.
body:
Context:
This doc captures a lightweight approach to instrumenting user-facing funnels (e.g., request -> auth -> routing -> model fanout -> response) so operators can trace a broken funnel end-to-end with minimal panels and an actionable triage checklist. Focus is latency attribution, cold-cache detection, and output-quality flagging at the operator surface.

Design principles (short):
- Funnel-first: model the user journey as a small set of funnel stages that are easy to read from a single dashboard row.
- Drill-to-trace: each funnel tile should link directly to a session-level trace with canonical span names and contextual tags.
- Cost-aware sampling: sample traces aggressively for high-error, high-latency requests and sparsely for healthy traffic.
- Lightweight panels: 4–6 tiles per funnel view (success rate, p95 latency, cold-cache rate, model-fanout ratio, output-quality-alerts, attendant errors).
- Operator verbs: each tile shows 1–2 suggested actions (e.g., "replay prompt", "pin fallback model", "check kv-warmth").

Funnel stages (canonical names to use in metrics/trace tags):
- client.request_received (entry)
- auth.check (auth)
- route.select (routing)
- model.prepare (prep: tokenizer/quantize)
- model.invoke (inference call(s); multiple spans for fanout)
- postprocess.apply (post-processing + rerank)
- response.sent (exit)

Metric definitions (recommended minimal set):
- funnel.requests.count: counter tagged by funnel_stage, tenant_id, model_variant, route_id
- funnel.latency.ms: histogram bucketing latency measured at funnel_stage (use consistent bucket boundaries across stages)
- funnel.error.count: counter with error_category (auth, route, model, postprocess, infra), severity (warning, critical)
- funnel.kv_cold.count: counter for cache-miss events when model.prepare occurs and kv cache is cold
- funnel.fanout.count: gauge/summary recording number of model invocations per request
- funnel.output-quality.flag: boolean/event when an automatic quality check fails (e.g., hallucination detector or length-truncation)
- funnel.replay_request.count: counter for operator-initiated replays (useful to correlate fixes)

Tagging and trace annotations:
- All spans should include: trace_id, session_id, request_id, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, seq_len_hint (if present), and kv_warmth_hint (warm|cold|unknown).
- model.invoke spans should annotate token_count, kv_hit_ratio (0.0–1.0), and any quantization profile used.
- Add an annotation field "operator_alert" for traces triggered by output-quality.flag or operator-created tickets.

Sampling strategy (practical):
- Full sampling for: any funnel.error.count where severity=critical, any output-quality.flag events, and any replay_request.
- 10% sampling for requests with latency > p95 and not otherwise flagged.
- Reservoir sample for steady-state traffic: maintain 1 trace per 1000 requests per tenant for long-tail visibility (adaptive per-tenant throttling).

Dashboard tiling (operator view):
- Top row: single-row funnel summary across stages (requests, success%, p95 latency, cold-rate) — clickable stage names.
- Middle row: fanout and model health (fanout distribution, average token throughput, per-variant p95).
- Bottom row: triage mini-logs (recent critical traces, recent output-quality flags, active replays).
- Each tile must show the recommended operator verb and a 1-line why (e.g., "Cold cache spike -> suggest: warm prefetch OR increase TTL").

Triage playbook (first 3 steps):
1) Identify affected tenants/routes via funnel.requests.count anomalies. If only 1 tenant, switch dashboard to tenant view.
2) Open linked trace from the highest-severity tile. Check model.invoke spans for kv_hit_ratio and token_count.
3) If kv_hit_ratio low and many model.invoke spans present, escalate to prefetched-kv team; temporarily route to fallback model if latency SLO breached.

Alerting heuristics (suggested):
- Alert when funnel.error.count/severity=critical spikes > 3x baseline for 5m AND p95 latency > SLO threshold.
- Alert on sustained increase in funnel.fanout.count per request (>1.8x baseline) because this indicates routing regressions or prompt duplication.
- Alert for output-quality.flag rate > 0.5% of requests for 30m.

Implementation notes / instrumenter checklist:
- Use canonical metric names above to simplify dashboard templates.
- Span naming must be consistent across languages: use dot-separated stage names.
- Ensure token_count and kv_hit_ratio are emitted as numeric metric tags when available (avoid embedding in free-text).
- Add a light-weight trace payload schema to the agent library; backward compatible with existing tracing.

Rollout checklist for a new funnel instrumented: (owner: eng-observability)
- [ ] Add server-side spans for funnel stages (PR and internal review).
- [ ] Add metrics emission for funnel.requests.count and funnel.latency.ms.
- [ ] Create dashboard fork and sanity panels in staging, validate links to traces.
- [ ] Run 48-hour dark traffic check for metric cardinality and query cost.
- [ ] Enable sampling policy and test trace retention/aggregation.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How fine-grained should fanout spans be for models with internal microcalls? (cost vs. debuggability)
- Is kv_hit_ratio better as a continuous tag or coarse buckets (low/medium/high) for trace payload size reasons?
- How do we classify borderline output-quality flags to avoid alert fatigue? Need small human-in-the-loop labelling before escalating to automated alerts.

Small experiments to run (next sprint):
- A/B test dashboard tile set with 4 vs 6 tiles and measure median triage time for simulated incidents.
- Evaluate 3 sampling policies (full-on-error, latency-threshold, reservoir) and measure trace storage cost over one week.
- Pilot an "operator-verb" UI hint in a single tenant's dashboard and collect feedback from 5 oncall rotations.

Notes to self: link to related artifacts above; follow up with product for output-quality definitions; sync with serving-runtime on consistent span names.

End of working notes. Expect to convert to a formal playbook after experiments and a short oncall pilot.
